# Topic at a Glance

> **One-sentence summary:** Viterbi selects the single most probable hidden-state path, whereas Forward--Backward sums across all paths to compute likelihoods and posterior state uncertainty.

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| **Biological question** | Which latent biological state best explains each observation, and how certain is that assignment? |
| **Computational problem** | Infer paths and probabilities in a hidden Markov model without enumerating exponentially many state sequences |
| **Method type** | Dynamic programming for probabilistic sequence models |
| **Input** | An HMM's start, transition, and emission probabilities plus an observed sequence |
| **Output** | Best path, sequence likelihood, and/or posterior probability for each state and position |
| **Bioinformatics uses** | Pairwise alignment, profile-HMM domain search, gene prediction, read-to-haplotype likelihoods |
| **Prerequisites** | [pairwise hidden Markov models](pairwise-hidden-markov-models.qmd), conditional probability, logarithms |

# One model, three inference questions

An HMM contains hidden states $z_1,\ldots,z_T$ and observations $x_1,\ldots,x_T$. With transition probability $a_{ij}=P(z_t=j\mid z_{t-1}=i)$ and emission probability $e_j(x_t)=P(x_t\mid z_t=j)$, a particular path has probability

$$
P(x,z)=P(z_1)e_{z_1}(x_1)\prod_{t=2}^{T}a_{z_{t-1},z_t}e_{z_t}(x_t).
$$

There are $K^T$ possible paths for $K$ states, so directly evaluating all paths is infeasible for realistic sequences. The shared-prefix structure makes dynamic programming possible.

| Question | Recurrence family | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Which one path is most probable? | Viterbi (max-product) | MAP state path and traceback |
| How probable are the observations under the model? | Forward (sum-product) | Likelihood $P(x)$ |
| How likely is state $j$ at position $t$? | Forward--Backward | Posterior $P(z_t=j\mid x)$ |

The distinction matters: a Viterbi label is a decision, not a probability that competing explanations vanished.

# The recurrences

## Viterbi decoding: retain the best predecessor

Let $\delta_t(j)$ be the probability of the most probable partial path that ends in state $j$ after observing $x_1,\ldots,x_t$. Then

$$
\delta_t(j)=e_j(x_t)\max_i\left[\delta_{t-1}(i)a_{ij}\right].
$$

Store the maximizing predecessor $\psi_t(j)$ for every cell. The largest final $\delta_T(j)$ identifies the final state; following the stored predecessors backward gives the path. In software, calculations usually use log probabilities, replacing products by sums and avoiding underflow.

## Forward likelihood: add every compatible predecessor

The Forward quantity $\alpha_t(j)$ is the probability of all partial paths ending in $j$:

$$
\alpha_t(j)=e_j(x_t)\sum_i\alpha_{t-1}(i)a_{ij}.
$$

Summing the final forward values gives $P(x)$. The recurrence looks like Viterbi, but replacing `max` with `sum` changes the scientific question: Forward rewards a model with many plausible paths, not only its best one.

## Backward pass and posterior states

The Backward value $\beta_t(i)$ is the probability of the remaining observations $x_{t+1:T}$ given state $i$ at time $t$:

$$
\beta_t(i)=\sum_j a_{ij}e_j(x_{t+1})\beta_{t+1}(j).
$$

Combining the two directions gives a normalized posterior:

$$
\gamma_t(j)=P(z_t=j\mid x)=\frac{\alpha_t(j)\beta_t(j)}{P(x)}.
$$

This quantity supports confidence tracks: for example, it can flag a weakly assigned profile-HMM alignment column even when Viterbi picks one state.

# Toy example: best path versus uncertainty

Imagine an HMM with states `C` (coding) and `N` (noncoding) that emits DNA bases. For the observations `A G`, suppose the model favors staying in the same state, while `A` slightly favors `N` and `G` slightly favors `C`.

```text
candidate paths:  N -> N     N -> C     C -> C     C -> N
Viterbi output:   chooses the single largest of these four probabilities
Forward output:   adds all four probabilities
Posterior at G:   asks how much of that total ends in C versus N
```

If `N -> C` barely beats `N -> N`, Viterbi reports a state transition at the second base. A posterior near 0.5 for `C` at that base communicates the more useful conclusion: the transition is uncertain. Conversely, a posterior can be high even if the globally best path contains a locally surprising choice, because it aggregates support across nearby paths.

# Bioinformatics applications

| Setting | Hidden states | Typical inference |
|---|---|---|
| [Pairwise HMM](pairwise-hidden-markov-models.qmd) | match and gap states | Viterbi alignment; Forward likelihood; column posteriors |
| [Profile HMM](profile-hidden-markov-models-for-protein-families.qmd) | match, insert, delete positions in a family | domain alignment and posterior confidence |
| Gene finding | coding frame, intron, intergenic states | best gene structure and state posterior track |
| Read likelihood models | alignment/error states | likelihood of a read under a candidate haplotype |

For an HMM with $K$ states and a length-$T$ sequence, the basic algorithms cost $O(TK^2)$ time. Sparse transitions, bands, and filtering reduce practical work. Forward values can underflow on long sequences, so implementations use scaling factors or log-space `log-sum-exp`; mixing unscaled Forward values with scaled Backward values produces incorrect posteriors.

# Practical interpretation and pitfalls

| Pitfall | Consequence | Better practice |
|---|---|---|
| Reporting only a Viterbi path | Ambiguous positions look falsely certain | Use posterior probabilities when the local assignment matters |
| Calling $P(x)$ a probability without context | Likelihoods are not normalized across different models or data lengths | Compare explicitly defined models or use calibrated scores |
| Decoding each position by its largest posterior state | The resulting labels may violate legal HMM transitions | Use Viterbi for one valid global path; use posterior decoding as a confidence summary |
| Ignoring model assumptions | A precise recurrence can still answer the wrong biological question | Inspect emissions, transitions, background model, and state topology |

# Connections

These recurrences provide the inference engine behind [pairwise HMMs](pairwise-hidden-markov-models.qmd) and [profile HMMs](profile-hidden-markov-models-for-protein-families.qmd). They also set up [expectation--maximization](expectation-maximization.qmd): Forward--Backward supplies expected hidden-state and transition counts, which are then used to re-estimate HMM parameters. Viterbi is analogous to a maximum-score dynamic program, while Forward--Backward is the probabilistic alternative that preserves uncertainty.

# Take-home Messages

1. Viterbi uses maximization to return one legal, most probable state path.
2. Forward sums over paths to compute the observation likelihood; Backward supplies compatible suffix probabilities.
3. Forward times Backward, normalized by the likelihood, yields posterior state confidence.
4. Dynamic programming replaces exponential path enumeration with $O(TK^2)$ computation, but it cannot compensate for a poorly specified HMM.
